heading.en: Why are you not a copy of your sibling?
heading.kn: ನೀವು ನಿಮ್ಮ ಒಡಹುಟ್ಟಿದವರ ನಕಲು ಏಕೆ ಅಲ್ಲ?

hook.en: Brothers and sisters share the same parents but look different. The reason lies in meiosis, where chromosomes pair up and swap pieces before they are shared out.
hook.kn: ಒಡಹುಟ್ಟಿದವರಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ತಂದೆ-ತಾಯಿ ಇದ್ದರೂ ಅವರು ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆಯಾಗಿ ಕಾಣುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣ ಅರ್ಧಸೂತ್ರ ವಿಭಜನೆ; ಅಲ್ಲಿ ವರ್ಣತಂತುಗಳು ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗಿ ತುಣುಕುಗಳನ್ನು ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: State the key features of meiosis.
Describe the five sub-stages of prophase I.
Describe metaphase I, anaphase I, telophase I and interkinesis.

narration.en: Brothers and sisters share the same parents but look different. The reason lies in meiosis, where chromosomes pair up and swap pieces before they are shared out.
narration.kn: ಒಡಹುಟ್ಟಿದವರಿಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ತಂದೆ-ತಾಯಿ ಇದ್ದರೂ ಅವರು ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆಯಾಗಿ ಕಾಣುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣ ಅರ್ಧಸೂತ್ರ ವಿಭಜನೆ; ಅಲ್ಲಿ ವರ್ಣತಂತುಗಳು ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗಿ ತುಣುಕುಗಳನ್ನು ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Meiosis is the specialised division that reduces the chromosome number by half and produces haploid daughter cells; it ensures the haploid phase in sexually reproducing organisms. It involves two sequential nuclear and cell division cycles (meiosis I and II) but only a single cycle of DNA replication, starts after the parental chromosomes have replicated in S phase, and involves pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between non-sister chromatids. Prophase I is long and has five sub-stages. Leptotene: chromosomes become gradually visible. Zygotene: homologous chromosomes pair (synapsis), aided by the synaptonemal complex; a pair is called a bivalent or tetrad. Pachytene: crossing over between non-sister chromatids, the exchange of genetic material catalysed by the enzyme recombinase, at recombination nodules; it is the stage when crossing over happens. Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and the homologues separate except at the X-shaped chiasmata; in oocytes of some vertebrates diplotene can last for months or years. Diakinesis: chiasmata terminalise, chromosomes are fully condensed, the spindle assembles, and the nucleolus and nuclear envelope disappear.

points.en: Leptotene → Zygotene (synapsis) → Pachytene (crossing over) → Diplotene (chiasmata) → Diakinesis (terminalisation).
Bivalent = tetrad: a pair of synapsed homologues.

narration.kn: ಅರ್ಧಸೂತ್ರ ವಿಭಜನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವರ್ಣತಂತು ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಅರ್ಧವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಪೂರ್ವಾವಸ್ಥೆ I ಗೆ ಐದು ಉಪಹಂತಗಳಿವೆ: ಲೆಪ್ಟೋಟೀನ್, ಜೈಗೋಟೀನ್, ಪ್ಯಾಕಿಟೀನ್, ಡಿಪ್ಲೋಟೀನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಡಯಾಕೈನೆಸಿಸ್. ಜೈಗೋಟೀನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮರೂಪಿ ವರ್ಣತಂತುಗಳು ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗುತ್ತವೆ, ಪ್ಯಾಕಿಟೀನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಅಡ್ಡ ವಿನಿಮಯ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: In metaphase I the bivalents align on the equatorial plate, with microtubules from opposite poles attaching to the kinetochores of the homologous chromosomes. In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate, while the sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. In telophase I the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear and cytokinesis follows, giving a dyad of cells. The stage between the two meiotic divisions is interkinesis; it is generally short-lived and there is no replication of DNA during it.

points.en: Anaphase I: homologues separate; this halves the chromosome number.
Sister chromatids stay together in anaphase I.

narration.kn: ಮಧ್ಯಾವಸ್ಥೆ I ನಲ್ಲಿ ದ್ವಿಯುಗ್ಮಗಳು ಮಧ್ಯಫಲಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಉತ್ತರಾವಸ್ಥೆ I ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮರೂಪಿ ವರ್ಣತಂತುಗಳು ಬೇರ್ಪಡುತ್ತವೆ, ಸಹೋದರ ಕ್ರೊಮ್ಯಾಟಿಡ್‌ಗಳು ಜೊತೆಯಲ್ಲೇ ಇರುತ್ತವೆ. ಅಂತರ ಚಲನಾವಸ್ಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ DNA ನಕಲು ಆಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

caption.en: Meiosis: homologous chromosomes pair, cross over, separate in meiosis I, and then the sister chromatids separate in meiosis II, giving four haploid cells.

problem.en: A plant cell has 2n = 24 chromosomes. How many bivalents form in zygotene, and how many chromosomes does each cell have at the end of meiosis I?

steps.en: A bivalent is one pair of homologous chromosomes, so bivalents = 24 ÷ 2 = 12.
In anaphase I homologues separate, so each pole receives one member of each pair.
Each cell after meiosis I has 12 chromosomes, each still made of two sister chromatids.

answer.en: 12 bivalents; 12 chromosomes per cell after meiosis I
